newsitem.title: INDIA: India govt borrowing will not pressure rates - RBI.
newsitem.headline: India govt borrowing will not pressure rates - RBI.

text.p: The Indian government's 1997/98 (April-March) borrowing requirement will not put upward pressure on interest rates or squeeze out corporates also seeking to raise funds, India's central bank governor said on Friday.

C.Rangarajan, governor of the Reserve Bank of India, said in a television interview on Star Plus channel that given monetary growth of around 16 percent corporate demand for funds should be satisfied.

"In terms of the borrowing programme I think what is envisaged is not very much higher. It is marginally higher than this year. I think we should be able to get the programme through without putting too much pressure on the interest rate," he said.
"I think we will be able to take care of the requirements of the commercial sector as well as the government sector."
